book_3b11.classification: A construction mechanism with hypotheses and required residue identities, worked out for symmetric-sextic-residual; not an automatic solve for all residual sectors.
book_3b11.quotient_chart: A finite symmetry quotient, exemplified by S3 x S3 on symmetric even sextics, gives F5 = 3 S x^2 + 3 T y^2 + H0(S,Q,T). A radial normal chart converts the ambient certificate equation into a divergence equation over quotient function field K5.
book_3b11.vertical_step: Explicit vertical Poisson fields with denominators dividing H0^2 absorb fiber-dependent source terms, leaving a horizontal residual.
book_3b11.horizontal_step: Lines on an auxiliary cubic threefold are imposed by four incidence equations. A quadratic extension and quadratic-cubic 5x5 Sylvester resultant followed by a norm give a univariate cover polynomial Pm.
book_3b11.required_conditions: Nondegenerate sheets/simple roots and the equality of complementary-pole residues with the horizontal residual are required. The section does not itself remove those checks for another target.
book_3b11.residue_step: The divergence contribution on each moving-line sheet is identified with a residue of a traced rational one-form. Global residues on P1 replace the inaccessible moving-sheet sum with local expansions at zero/infinity and a power-sum trace over spurious poles.
book_3b11.descent_and_lift: After the residue sum matches the horizontal residual, adding the vertical field, finite normalized-trace descent, and an ambient Piola lift produce the sextic certificate.
book_3b11.constructive_scope: The text explicitly says rational dependence of the sheet coordinates on the simple cover root makes the summed horizontal field Galois-invariant in K5^4 and constructively determines a cleared witness (N,D). It avoids multiplying out degree-m norms of all sheet denominators. This is an algebraic/trace representation statement, not evidence that an expanded polynomial witness file was exported.

book_5_8.classification: Exact identity-verification methods and local residue computation; no new target acceptance is inferred from this prose.
book_5_8.kronecker_grid: Mixed-radix encoding with explicit degree and coefficient-mass bounds; a hybrid two-variable Kronecker substitution plus a sufficiently large centered grid in the third variable proves an identity by positional uniqueness, injectivity and root counting. PolyOps/PolyOpsRel/letB share the program across symbolic, integer and bound-tracking backends.
book_5_8.laurent_jets: Under stated quadratic Hensel hypotheses, branch maps to K((t)) support leading and two-term Laurent jets. Dual numbers propagate the needed coefficients. Five-point interpolation handles bounded-degree numerators with scaled valuation bounds.
book_5_8.spurious_pole_weights: For squarefree Q coprime to H, a Bezout relation replaces 1/H at roots of Q. Lagrange-Euler power sums and exact recurrences evaluate the residue sum by finite coefficient-weight contraction without adjoining the roots.

new_report_scope.author: Robert Joseph (Robertboy18)
new_report_scope.claim_status: Unfinished author-reported degree-six analysis. The edited post explicitly says proofs have no independent review and nothing is in Lean, highlighting bounds 44 and 36 as claims to check.
new_report_scope.conditional_core: A proposed degree-six certificate would force the source class into a proper deck-stable sub-Hodge structure of the sigma-odd H3 of the core threefold. Absence of such a substructure, or sufficient simplicity of the proposed 48-dimensional abelian variety, remains unproved.
new_report_scope.dimension_scope: Bounds 44 and 36 are stated for the deck-nontrivial part of H^{1,0} of a resolution of T intersect {D=0}; comparison dimension 48 is the sigma-odd H^{2,1}(T). They are not dimensions of all H1 or all H3.
new_report_scope.prior_object_distinction: The earlier post19694056 reports absolute simplicity of a three-dimensional binary Prym; it does not settle the new proposed 48-dimensional core condition.
new_report_scope.restricted_results: Claims pencil/singularity restrictions and exclusions for selected denominator shapes. Reducible denominators without linear factors and several irreducible singular cases remain open. No full degree-six impossibility claim or target solve.
